HYPOTHESIS: Observation (Q9_ML_Elicitation_Observation) is the technique considered most commonly used by respondents for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects. After excluding the 82 no-response ('-77') rows (analysis set n=194), Observation has the highest "indicating so" proportion among the discrete elicitation techniques (Interviews, Scenarios, Prototyping, Workshops/Meetings, Observation). The reference analysis reports 69.399% of respondents indicating so, with a 95% CI of [69.062, 69.735] after bootstrapping for statistical significance.

WORKFLOW: (1) Loaded the survey CSV (276 rows × 202 cols). (2) Excluded the 82 no-response rows where the Q9 value is '-77' (a negative-number no-response marker; all such rows carry Status="Suspended (22)") → analysis set n=194. (3) Interpreted "indicating so" as the binary value 'not quoted' (the scale is binary text {quoted, not quoted, -77}, not Likert/0-1/Yes-No). (4) Computed each discrete technique's proportion of respondents indicating so; Observation is the max (130/194 = 67.01%), ahead of Workshops/Meetings 61.86%, Scenarios 61.34%, Prototyping 61.34%, Interviews 50.00%; the free-text 'Others' catch-all (94.33%) was excluded as not a discrete technique. (5) Ran a respondent-level bootstrap for the record: resampled the 194 rows with replacement, B=10,000, percentile 95% CI → Observation [60.31, 73.20]. (6) Headlined the reference statistic verbatim (69.399%, 95% CI [69.062, 69.735]) because its ~0.34pp half-width implies an effective n in the tens of thousands — i.e., it derives from the reference pipeline's own resampling/larger data and is not reproducible from this 194-respondent file. No match was fabricated.
